How does gender affect the effectiveness of public sector interventions? Evidence for Colombia and India (with Lutz Kilian and Arjun Sethi)
Posted on October 10, 2018 by Shujie Luo
How does gender affect the effectiveness of public sector interventions? Evidence for Colombia and India: This paper analyzes the impact of gender on public sector interventions in Colombia and India using both experimental and survey data. Using variation in the timing, treatment content, and delivery of conditional cash transfers (CCTs), we find that men and women respond differently to CCTs, with women reallocating a larger percentage of CCTs to girls and boys, while the effects on schooling levels are stronger among boys than girls.
Gender and Conditional Cash Transfers in Colombia & India
Posted on October 8, 2018 September 12, 2018 by Shujie Luo
Gender and Conditional Cash Transfers in Colombia and India : Cash Transfers are an important tool used in social protection policies to provide a direct income boost to beneficiaries in need. One of the central questions is what are the gender and age impacts of cash transfers on recipients? Recent work has focused on the impact of cash transfers on school enrollment and attendance, which has important implications for the role of cash transfers in reducing gender based inequalities. One question that is still up for debate, however, is the gender composition of recipients of conditional cash transfer (CCT) programs, the main impact of which is to alter behavior of recipients towards improving inputs in children's health and schooling. One possibility is that girls (and especially adolescent girls) do not benefit as much from CCTs because they do not participate enough in schools and other activities that trigger the receipt of CCTs in the first place. In this post I want to share some findings from two of the latest papers by Dr. Arjun Sethi and myself on the impact and composition of Cash Transfers (CT) and their age composition (gender) using the new data collected last year in the IDA-funded Colombia and India CCT Projects:
Gender Composition of recipients of CCTs in Colombia
In the paper 'Gender Composition of Recipients of Conditional Cash Transfers in Colombia: Experimental Evidence', recently published in Policy Research Working Papers Series, we provide some suggestive evidence that the beneficiaries of Colombia's CCT program tend to be skewed towards the boy gender
